summary: Renewal/check-in focused on adding Dedicated capacity and activating EU region. Customer wants scope of Dedicated pool, burst mechanics, VPC/KMS details, SOC2 implications, and a short benchmark window. Agreed to pricing revision and a pilot benchmark. Next call to finalize contract amendment.
topics: EU region onramp (eu-west1) and data residency
Private deployment / VPC networking and KMS integration
transcript:
[00:00] Morgan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. this is Morgan from Redwood, joined by Priya and Diego on the engineering side. alex, ruth, hi, can you hear us okay?
[00:12] Alex Chen: yeah — loud and clear, thanks. um, big agenda item is the renewal next month and we want to lock in capacity and start ramping eu.
[00:20] Morgan Lee: perfect. real quick run-through: we heard you want Dedicated for predictable throughput, eu region for residency, and a short pilot to validate latency and cost, right?
[00:30] Ruth Park: correct. cost is a big one, but also tail latency for our user flows. we saw some spikes in the last quarter with the hosted endpoints.
[00:45] Priya Nair: got it. the Dedicated pool gives you reserved GPU capacity and predictable p99s; we can also set autoscale and burst rules. note that burst is metered differently, that's important for TCO.
[01:05] Samir Patel: just to clarify, burst is like transient extra capacity, but billing is per-minute? i thought it was per-hour..
[01:12] Diego Alvarez: it's a hybrid — burst uses reserved spare nodes first, then on-demand at minute granularity. the cost sheet shows effective per-token delta but we can model your patterns.
[01:30] Jamie Ortiz: timeline — we have an internal deadline to cutover user flows by end of october, so want the pilot and contract signed before then.
[01:42] Morgan Lee: that's tight but doable. we'll prioritize the benchmark week and the contract amendment. 
[01:50] Alex Chen: security — we need VPC/private control plane and KMS support. are HSM integrations available?
[01:58] Priya Nair: we support customer-managed KMS integrations — HSM providers via standard KMS APIs. for VPC we offer private deployment with customer-managed peering, but there are a few networking checks (route tables, MTU, egress).
[02:15] Ruth Park: and SOC2 — we're bringing security in. do you have an updated SOC2 report and audit logs retention details?
[02:22] Morgan Lee: yes, SOC2 report is in the security pack — i'll share the docs. audit logs can be pushed to your logging endpoint; retention is configurable (we'll include options).
[02:33] Samir Patel: any constraints on model variants? we use a quantized variant (8-bit) in prod, does Redwood Dedicated support that?
[02:40] Priya Nair: yes, our runtime supports quantized models and we can pin model versions; kernel selection will optimize for your sequence lengths but sometimes we recommend a small tuning step.
[02:52] Alex Chen: the EU region — do you guarantee data residency? we need to ensure tokens and logs don't cross into usa.
[03:00] Diego Alvarez: for Private deployments in eu-west we can keep control plane in your VPC and configure region-level routing; logging and metrics can be stored in eu-only buckets. we'll document exact flow.
[03:12] Ruth Park: great. okay, on pricing: last year we had a usage-heavy month and the surge killed us. can you give a comparison of hosted vs dedicated buckets?
[03:22] Morgan Lee: absolutely — i'll send a TCO sheet showing committed capacity pricing, burst rates, and an example with your monthly token baseline. for reference, competitors like CloudText sometimes look cheaper on list price but they don't include KV-cache optimizations we run, so effective cost differs.
[03:37] Alex Chen: KV-cash? (laughs) i think you mean KV cache, yeah — caching mattered a lot for our prompt patterns.
[03:44] Priya Nair: yeah, KV cache — our prefix/KV caching helps with multi-turn chat. we'll include expected hit rates in the benchmark plan.
[03:55] Jamie Ortiz: benchmark — what do you need from us?
[04:00] Priya Nair: ideally: a sample corpus (5000 sessions), expected QPS, auth creds for test routing, and SSO metadata for simulating real user flows. we'll run a two-day window with both hosted and dedicated configurations.
[04:12] Samir Patel: ok we'll produce that. do you need real customer PII in the samples?
[04:18] Diego Alvarez: no, please scrub PII — we only need shape and size. hashed tokens are fine.
[04:23] Alex Chen: contract amendment — can we add language for a 12-month committed pool with a mid-term uplift clause?
[04:30] Morgan Lee: yes, we can draft an amendment: committed capacity + uplift options at pre-negotiated bands. we'll add an SLA target and a canary fallback policy.
[04:40] Ruth Park: what about failover region? if eu goes down, traffic will route to us-east? we need graceful degradation not massive latency spikes.
[04:48] Priya Nair: we support failover policies by route: latency-first or cost-first. for you we recommend latency-first with model fallbacks. that will route to closest compatible model in alternate region and maintain p95 SLA while accepting higher cost.
[05:05] Samir Patel: fine. one question — how much lead time to provision Dedicated nodes in eu-west?
[05:10] Diego Alvarez: typical lead time is 5-8 business days for Dedicated pool staging, less if we reuse existing geocapacity. but for private VPC onboarding add configuration time (about 7-10 days).
[05:25] Alex Chen: so to meet end-of-october we need to kick off next week.
[05:30] Morgan Lee: agreed. we'll schedule the benchmark the week of 2027-09-20 as discussed.
[05:35] Jamie Ortiz: are there any legal/contract items that block signing quickly? procurement wants net30 and some data residency language.
[05:42] Morgan Lee: procurement standard is net30; we can surface residency clauses in amendment. legal generally takes 1-2 weeks once we align commercials.
[05:50] Ruth Park: ok. can you also share a sample runbook for oncall/ops for region failover?
[05:56] Priya Nair: yes, we'll attach a short ops runbook showing rollback, model fallback, and tracing hooks.
[06:04] Alex Chen: on the benchmarking — tail latency is huge for our UX. can you simulate 99.9% tail?
[06:10] Priya Nair: we can target p99.9 with load profiles, and capture tail-latency histograms. we'll give you both raw logs and aggregated views.
[06:18] Samir Patel: if we see persistent tail spikes, what's the usual mitigation?
[06:22] Diego Alvarez: common fixes: increase reserved pool, tune batch windows, enable prefix caching, or use a lower-latency model variant for critical flows. we can run an A/B canary during the pilot.
[06:35] Alex Chen: regarding SSO, our identity is SAML 2.0 with idp metadata, do you support SCIM provisioning?
[06:43] Morgan Lee: yes SCIM supported for user provisioning, SAML for SSO. we'll need metadata and an admin account.
[06:50] Jamie Ortiz: anything else on data protection — encryption at rest and in transit?
[06:54] Priya Nair: both — TLS in transit, and at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys if you want. HSM-backed KMS is available per your vendor.
[07:05] Ruth Park: we talked about observability — how granular are cost breakdowns? per-route? per-token?
[07:11] Morgan Lee: console gives token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency charts. we can also surface per-model and per-prompt group metrics.
[07:21] Alex Chen: ok good. i want the cost view for our two main flows: query and assistant.
[07:25] Morgan Lee: we'll include that in the TCO sheet.
[07:30] Jamie Ortiz: competitors — we've seen a pitch from NimbusAI that emphasizes pricing, but lacked deployment options. anything we should be aware of?
[07:38] Diego Alvarez: competitors often trade off routing flexibility and caching. Redwood's differentiator is unified runtime and the private options; we'll document those tradeoffs for your execs.
[07:50] Alex Chen: sounds good. so immediate checklist: pricing, benchmark, SSO/KMS docs, amendment draft.
[07:58] Morgan Lee: yes. i'll summarize and send after the call. Priya will own the benchmark orchestration.
[08:05] Priya Nair: we'll put a proposed schedule in the calendar and reserve nodes.
[08:10] Ruth Park: thanks. quick nit — billing alignment, our finance wants monthly statements and a single invoice.
[08:16] Morgan Lee: no problem, we can do consolidated monthly invoicing and show committed vs burst lines.
[08:22] Samir Patel: one last ops question: tracing hooks — can we forward traces to our jaeger/tempo stack?
[08:28] Diego Alvarez: yes we support OTLP export to your tracing collector; we'll include sample config for tempo/jaeger.
[08:36] Alex Chen: great. anything else?
[08:39] Jamie Ortiz: not from product.
[08:41] Ruth Park: we'll aim to have SSO and sample corpus by friday.
[08:45] Morgan Lee: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and pricing today. talk soon.
[08:52] END OF CALL

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard terms (KV cash -> KV cache) and abbreviations; speaker labels approximate.
